```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A directory audit asks whether a source contains the physician, whether a
field is populated, whether reported values agree across sources, and whether
independent evidence confirms those values. Each question has its own
denominator. This vignette runs all 19 public functions and both print methods
added in the 72-hour window ending November 8, 2026, at 7:26 p.m. Mountain Time.
All examples are synthetic. Source names illustrate the workflow. Field
availability and lineage in a real study come from its dated extracts and
documentation.

## Audit a snapshot

Start with a physician-year frame, an index of records actually delivered, and
metadata declaring the completeness of each extract. The dictionary separates
practice and mailing fields and records shared source lineage. Review
requirements and normalization rules before interpreting a field as usable.

```{r audit-frame}
frame <- tibble::tibble(npi = base::as.character(1:6), year = 2024L)
registry <- base::c("nppes", "pecos", "dac")
record_index <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(frame, source = "nppes"),
  dplyr::mutate(frame[1:5, ], source = "pecos"),
  dplyr::mutate(frame, source = "dac")
)
manifest <- tibble::tibble(
  year = 2024L, source = registry, extract_complete = TRUE
)
study_populations <- mysteryroster::attribute_analysis_populations(
  frame, record_index, manifest, pair = base::c("nppes", "pecos"),
  accuracy_sample = frame[1:5, ]
)
dictionary <- mysteryroster::attribute_field_dictionary(
  tibble::tibble(
    attribute = "practice_zip5", definition = "ZIP of a practice site",
    location_role = "practice", normalizer = "zip5"
  ),
  sources = registry,
  lineage_groups = base::list(medicare_enrollment = base::c("pecos", "dac"))
)
dictionary[, base::c("source", "attribute", "lineage", "requirement")]
dplyr::count(study_populations$coverage, source, record_status)
```

The synthetic DAC extract lacks the ZIP column. The NPPES record for physician
4 has an explicit blank ZIP. PECOS has a record for that physician but no ZIP
assertion. Keep these three cases separate from an absent physician record.

```{r presence-and-agreement}
source_fields <- tibble::tibble(
  year = 2024L, source = registry, attribute = "practice_zip5",
  field_available = base::c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)
)
nppes_zip <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = base::c("1", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"), year = 2024L,
  practice_zip5 = base::c(
    "80204", "80045", "80045", "80218", NA, "80521", "80903"
  )
)
pecos_zip <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = base::c("1", "2", "3", "5"), year = 2024L,
  practice_zip5 = base::c("80204", "80045", "80204", "80521")
)
claims <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nppes = nppes_zip, pecos = pecos_zip, .id = "source"
) |>
  dplyr::rename(value = practice_zip5) |>
  dplyr::mutate(attribute = "practice_zip5")

presence <- mysteryroster::attribute_record_presence(
  study_populations$coverage, dictionary, source_fields, claims
)
dplyr::count(presence, source, completeness_eligible, field_status)

agreement <- mysteryroster::attribute_set_agreement(
  base::list(nppes = nppes_zip, pecos = pecos_zip),
  attribute = "practice_zip5"
)
agreement[, base::c("id", "any_shared", "same_set")]
agreement_summary <- mysteryroster::attribute_set_agreement_summary(agreement)
agreement_summary
```

Physician 1 shares one ZIP between sources but has a second ZIP in NPPES. That
counts as an any-shared match and a complete-set disagreement. Agreement
requires usable values from both sources and describes what the sources report.

## Link enrollment to practice sites

An individual enrollment and a reassignment to a group can each lead to sites.
The group has two sites in this example. Physician 3's enrollment has no
matching location record. Keep the link path and inspect unmatched enrollments
before interpreting the site list. Administrative linkage alone leaves
clinical presence unverified.

```{r enrollment-linkage}
individual <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = base::c("1", "3"), year = 2024L,
  enrollment_id = base::c("individual_a", "individual_unmatched")
)
reassignment <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = "1", year = 2024L, enrollment_id = "group_a"
)
locations <- tibble::tibble(
  year = 2024L,
  enrollment_id = base::c("individual_a", "group_a", "group_a"),
  location_id = base::c("direct_site", "group_site_1", "group_site_2"),
  practice_zip5 = base::c("80204", "80204", "80045")
)
linkage <- mysteryroster::attribute_enrollment_locations(
  individual, reassignment, locations
)
linkage$links[, base::c("id", "linkage_path", "location_id")]
linkage$unmatched_enrollments
```

## Freeze the questions and account for nonresponse

The questionnaire creates one question per distinct assertion. Store that
table before fieldwork and record answers by question ID. Here, telephone
verification confirms both listed ZIPs for physician 1 and finds an error
for physician 2. Physician 3 has an unsuccessful contact attempt, physician 4
has a missing ZIP, and physician 5 is never called.

```{r verification}
mysteryroster::attribute_verification_codebook()

sample <- dplyr::mutate(
  frame[1:5, ], stratum = "overlap",
  weight = base::c(1, 3, 2, 4, 6),
  eligibility_status = base::c(
    "eligible", "eligible", "eligible", "eligible", "unknown"
  )
)
frozen <- mysteryroster::attribute_verification_questionnaire(
  sample, dplyr::filter(claims, source == "nppes")
)
answered <- dplyr::filter(frozen, id %in% base::c("1", "2"))
answers <- tibble::tibble(
  question_id = answered$question_id,
  answer = base::ifelse(answered$id == "1", "correct", "never_correct"),
  verified_at = base::as.Date("2024-11-15"),
  respondent_role = "office_staff", verification_method = "telephone"
)
contacts <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = base::c("1", "2", "3"), year = 2024L,
  contacted_at = base::as.Date("2024-11-15"),
  channel = "telephone",
  outcome = base::c("reached", "reached", "no_answer")
)
audit <- mysteryroster::attribute_nonresponse_audit(
  sample, frozen, answers, contacts
)
audit$providers[, base::c("id", "n_attempts", "response_status")]
audit$response_rates
```

Specify the independent methods allowed by the study protocol. The adapter
returns one row per sampled physician-year and target, including explicit
exclusions. Its eligible rows carry the original sampling weights. Include
every source and attribute pair represented in the audit when defining
targets, then analyze each pair separately.

```{r weighted-validity}
classified <- mysteryroster::attribute_verification_status(
  audit, tibble::tibble(source = "nppes", attribute = "practice_zip5"),
  independent_methods = "telephone"
)
classified$fields[, base::c(
  "id", "weight", "listing_status", "exclusion_reason"
)]
design <- mysteryroster::listing_validity_design(classified$validity)
mysteryroster::validity_estimates(design, definitive_only = TRUE)
mysteryroster::validity_sensitivity_bounds(
  design, denominator = "all_sampled"
)
```

The definitive estimate uses listings with a confirmed outcome. The bounds
include attempted and unattempted eligible listings and assign unknown
outcomes to the two extremes. A missing ZIP is excluded from accuracy for
listed values and still contributes to the completeness analysis above.

## Write the audit paragraph

Pass the underlying tables to the prose function. This paragraph describes
coverage, completeness, agreement, linkage, and response. Report the weighted
verification estimates alongside it as a separate result.

```{r audit-prose, results="asis"}
paragraph <- mysteryroster::attribute_oig_audit_prose(
  presence, agreement_summary, year = 2024L,
  source_a = "nppes", source_b = "pecos", attribute = "practice_zip5",
  attribute_label = "practice ZIP codes",
  linkage = linkage$links, nonresponse = audit
)
base::cat(paragraph, "\n")
```

## Add payment and claims evidence to the snapshot

The three extracts add different kinds of evidence. Keep their row grain,
identifier role, and address provenance in the audit.

| Extract | What to retain | How to use it |
|:--|:--|:--|
| [CMS Open Payments][op] | Covered recipient NPI, program year, recipient business ZIP | Payment-recipient observation and a reported business address |
| [HHS/DOGE Medicaid Provider Spending by HCPCS][doge] | Billing NPI, servicing NPI, HCPCS, claim month | Claims observations by NPI role. The release has no address field. |
| [Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service][medicare] | Rendering NPI, service year, HCPCS, place-of-service category, provider ZIP | Fee-for-service Part B activity. The ZIP comes from NPPES and describes the provider address. |

[op]: https://openpaymentsdata.cms.gov/datasets/download
[doge]: https://opendata.hhs.gov/datasets/medicaid-provider-spending/
[medicare]: https://data.cms.gov/provider-summary-by-type-of-service/medicare-physician-other-practitioners/medicare-physician-other-practitioners-by-provider-and-service//data

The [Open Payments dictionary][op-dd] describes `Recipient_Zip_Code` as a
recipient's primary practice or business ZIP. The
[Medicare Provider and Service dictionary][medicare-dd] defines
`Rndrng_Prvdr_Zip5` using NPPES and separately defines the place-of-service
category. Treat an NPPES and Medicare provider ZIP match as one address
lineage. A facility category alone does not locate the site of care.

[op-dd]: https://www.cms.gov/files/document/open-payments-methodology-data-dictionary-document-january-2026.pdf
[medicare-dd]: https://data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2025-03/bbb1e50e-5ba8-42ed-b072-18368b6f37f9/MUP_PHY_RY25_20250312_DD_PRV_SVC_508.pdf

These synthetic extracts use study-normalized names and ZIP5 values. In a
real import, keep the release vintage alongside the program or service
period and preserve identifiers and ZIPs as character strings. HHS describes
the Medicaid file as a suppressed aggregation, so absence from the public
file leaves activity unknown. A billing organization outside the physician
frame stays outside the frame. A billing NPI alone does not identify the
clinician who performed a service.

```{r federal-extracts}
payments <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = base::c("1", "1", "5"), year = 2024L,
  recipient_business_zip5 = base::c("80204", "80204", "80521")
)
medicaid <- tibble::tibble(
  billing_npi = base::c("900", "900", "2"),
  servicing_npi = base::c("3", "3", NA_character_),
  claim_month = base::c("2024-01", "2024-02", "2024-02"),
  hcpcs = "99213"
)
medicare <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = base::c("1", "1", "3"), year = 2024L, hcpcs = "99213",
  place_of_service = base::c("F", "O", "O"),
  nppes_provider_zip5 = base::c("80204", "80204", "80218")
)

```

```{r federal-roles}
known_month <- !base::is.na(medicaid$claim_month)
valid_month <- base::grepl(
  "^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$", medicaid$claim_month
)
if (base::any(known_month & !valid_month)) {
  base::stop("claim_month must use YYYY-MM with month 01 through 12.",
             call. = FALSE)
}

medicaid_roles <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  billing = dplyr::transmute(medicaid, npi = billing_npi, claim_month),
  servicing = dplyr::transmute(medicaid, npi = servicing_npi, claim_month),
  .id = "npi_role"
) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    npi, year = base::as.integer(base::substr(claim_month, 1, 4)),
    npi_role
  ) |>
  dplyr::semi_join(frame, by = base::c("npi", "year")) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
medicaid_roles
```

Collapse rows to one physician-year per source for coverage. Repeated
payments or service codes do not multiply physicians. The Medicaid role
table above still distinguishes how the physician was observed. For these
three extracts the example uses conservative non-observation statuses.
Declare source-years independently of observed records so an extract
with zero matched physicians remains in the coverage table. A missing
public payment or claim leaves practice location unknown. Medicaid rows
with missing months do not establish dated activity. A supplied month must
be a valid YYYY-MM value before it can enter the annual coverage table.

```{r federal-coverage}
federal_index <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  open_payments = dplyr::select(payments, npi, year),
  medicaid_spending = dplyr::select(medicaid_roles, npi, year),
  medicare_provider_service = dplyr::select(medicare, npi, year),
  .id = "source"
) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
federal_manifest <- tibble::tibble(
  year = 2024L,
  source = base::c(
    "open_payments", "medicaid_spending", "medicare_provider_service"
  ),
  extract_complete = FALSE
)
expanded_manifest <- dplyr::bind_rows(manifest, federal_manifest)
expanded_populations <- mysteryroster::attribute_analysis_populations(
  frame, dplyr::bind_rows(record_index, federal_index), expanded_manifest,
  pair = base::c("nppes", "pecos")
)
dplyr::count(expanded_populations$coverage, source, record_status)
```

Audit the two address columns under their own field definitions. Medicaid
contributes to observed-record coverage and has no eligible denominator for
either ZIP field. The Medicare ZIP's lineage applies to the address, while
the Medicare rendering record remains a separate utilization observation.

```{r federal-field-presence}
federal_fields <- tibble::tibble(
  attribute = base::c("recipient_business_zip5", "nppes_provider_zip5"),
  definition = base::c("Recipient business ZIP", "NPPES provider ZIP"),
  location_role = base::c("recipient_business", "registry_provider"),
  normalizer = "zip5"
)
expanded_dictionary <- mysteryroster::attribute_field_dictionary(
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    dplyr::distinct(dictionary, attribute, definition, location_role,
                    normalizer),
    federal_fields
  ),
  sources = expanded_manifest$source,
  lineage_groups = base::list(
    medicare_enrollment = base::c("pecos", "dac"),
    nppes_address = base::c("nppes", "medicare_provider_service")
  )
)
federal_availability <- dplyr::filter(
  expanded_dictionary, attribute %in% federal_fields$attribute
) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    year = 2024L, source, attribute,
    field_available =
      (source == "open_payments" & attribute == "recipient_business_zip5") |
      (source == "medicare_provider_service" &
         attribute == "nppes_provider_zip5")
  )
expanded_availability <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  source_fields,
  dplyr::mutate(federal_manifest, attribute = "practice_zip5",
                field_available = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::select(-extract_complete),
  federal_availability
)
expanded_claims <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  claims,
  dplyr::transmute(payments, npi, year, source = "open_payments",
                   attribute = "recipient_business_zip5",
                   value = recipient_business_zip5),
  dplyr::transmute(medicare, npi, year, source = "medicare_provider_service",
                   attribute = "nppes_provider_zip5",
                   value = nppes_provider_zip5)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
expanded_presence <- mysteryroster::attribute_record_presence(
  expanded_populations$coverage, expanded_dictionary,
  expanded_availability, expanded_claims
)
expanded_presence |>
  dplyr::filter(source %in% federal_manifest$source, record_present) |>
  dplyr::count(source, attribute, completeness_eligible, field_status)
```

### CMS resources for Medicare Part B and Part D

| Resource | Use in a physician audit |
|:--|:--|
| [Part B: Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service][medicare] | Use the rendering NPI and service year to observe published Original Medicare fee-for-service Part B activity. Keep HCPCS and facility or non-facility category for service-level analyses. |
| [Part D: Prescribers by Provider][part-d-provider] | Use the prescriber NPI and year for a provider-level observation of prescriptions dispensed under Part D, including refills. |
| [Part D: Prescribers by Provider and Drug][part-d-drug] | Use when the drug matters. Collapse drug rows to one prescriber-year before counting physician coverage. |

The Part B provider ZIP and the Part D by-provider address both come from
NPPES. Treat those address fields as one lineage alongside NPPES. The
service and dispensing records are distinct activity observations. Part D
prescriber geography does not identify the dispensing pharmacy or locate
the clinical encounter. Keep the two program populations separate when
interpreting missing records because eligibility, utilization, and public
release rules differ.

[Part B data dictionary][medicare-dd] ·
[Part D by-provider data dictionary][part-d-dd]

[part-d-provider]: https://data.cms.gov/provider-summary-by-type-of-service/medicare-part-d-prescribers/medicare-part-d-prescribers-by-provider
[part-d-drug]: https://data.cms.gov/provider-summary-by-type-of-service/medicare-part-d-prescribers/medicare-part-d-prescribers-by-provider-and-drug/api-docs
[part-d-dd]: https://data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2025-04/MUP_DPR_RY25_20250401_DD_PRV_508.pdf

### Map the CMS columns to the audit

For physician-year coverage, use **Part B by Provider and Service** and
**Part D by Provider**. The latter already summarizes prescriptions by
prescriber. Use the drug-level Part D file when the analysis needs drug
identity. The table below uses the [Part B][medicare-dd] and
[Part D by-provider][part-d-dd] dictionaries. Check the headers for the
specific release you import.

| Audit field | Part B by Provider and Service | Part D by Provider | How to use it |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Physician identifier | `Rndrng_NPI` | `Prscrbr_NPI` | Read as character. Match to the physician frame by NPI and year. |
| Individual or organization | `Rndrng_Prvdr_Ent_Cd` | `Prscrbr_Ent_Cd` | Keep `I` for individual clinicians. The study frame defines which individuals are physicians in scope. |
| Activity year | Year of the selected annual CMS file | Year of the selected annual CMS file | Assign the activity year from the selected release and retain the download vintage separately. |
| Activity detail | `HCPCS_Cd`, `Place_Of_Srvc` | Provider-level summary | Part B has separate HCPCS and facility/non-facility rows. A place-of-service category does not identify the facility address. |
| Activity count | `Tot_Srvcs` | `Tot_Clms` | Keep these separate. The first counts services at the Part B row grain. The second counts dispensed claims including refills. |
| Beneficiary count | `Tot_Benes` | `Tot_Benes` | Interpret at the published grain. The same person may contribute to several Part B rows. Part D beneficiary counts can be suppressed. |
| Street | `Rndrng_Prvdr_St1`, `Rndrng_Prvdr_St2` | `Prscrbr_St1`, `Prscrbr_St2` | NPPES provider address, with shared provenance. |
| City | `Rndrng_Prvdr_City` | `Prscrbr_City` | NPPES provider city. |
| State | `Rndrng_Prvdr_State_Abrvtn` or `Rndrng_Prvdr_State_Abvtn` in CMS documentation | `Prscrbr_State_Abrvtn` | Check the Part B download header before mapping the state field. |
| ZIP5 | `Rndrng_Prvdr_Zip5` | `Prscrbr_Zip5` | Read as character to retain leading zeros. Track under the NPPES address lineage. |

The [earlier Part B dictionary][medicare-dd-earlier] and the linked Part B
dictionary spell the state variable differently. In an import, verify the
header against the file you actually downloaded. For coverage, count a
physician once per source and activity year. The public release can omit
low-volume records, so keep absent physician-years as unobserved.

[medicare-dd-earlier]: https://data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2020-09/Medicare%20Physician%20%26%20Other%20Practitioners%20-%20by%20Provider%20and%20Service-Data-Dictionary.pdf

This example uses synthetic rows with CMS column names. It produces a
Medicare activity index and a separate address ledger. The Part D example
is a companion to the six-source audit above.

```{r medicare-dictionary-mapping}
part_b_csv <- tibble::tibble(
  Rndrng_NPI = base::c("1", "1", "3"),
  Rndrng_Prvdr_Ent_Cd = "I",
  HCPCS_Cd = base::c("99213", "99214", "99213"),
  Place_Of_Srvc = base::c("F", "O", "O"),
  Tot_Srvcs = base::c(18L, 26L, 15L),
  Rndrng_Prvdr_City = "Denver", Rndrng_Prvdr_Zip5 = "80204"
)
part_d_csv <- tibble::tibble(
  Prscrbr_NPI = base::c("2", "3"),
  Prscrbr_Ent_Cd = "I", Tot_Clms = base::c(32L, 19L),
  Prscrbr_City = base::c("Aurora", "Denver"),
  Prscrbr_Zip5 = base::c("80045", "80204")
)
part_b_rows <- part_b_csv |>
  dplyr::filter(Rndrng_Prvdr_Ent_Cd == "I") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    npi = Rndrng_NPI, year = 2024L, hcpcs = HCPCS_Cd,
    place_of_service = Place_Of_Srvc, services = Tot_Srvcs,
    city = Rndrng_Prvdr_City, zip5 = Rndrng_Prvdr_Zip5
  )
part_d_rows <- part_d_csv |>
  dplyr::filter(Prscrbr_Ent_Cd == "I") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    npi = Prscrbr_NPI, year = 2024L, dispensed_claims = Tot_Clms,
    city = Prscrbr_City, zip5 = Prscrbr_Zip5
  )

medicare_address_ledger <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  medicare_part_b = dplyr::select(part_b_rows, npi, year, city, zip5),
  medicare_part_d = dplyr::select(part_d_rows, npi, year, city, zip5),
  .id = "source"
) |>
  dplyr::semi_join(frame, by = base::c("npi", "year")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(address_lineage = "nppes_address") |>
  dplyr::distinct()

medicare_activity_index <- medicare_address_ledger |>
  dplyr::distinct(npi, year, source)

medicare_activity_index
medicare_address_ledger
```

## Follow the same attribute across years

Use a separate panel with one practice-state value per physician-year and
source. Coverage counts populated values against an explicit universe.
Churn counts changes between consecutive observed years. A registry can
have high coverage and high churn, and churn can reflect actual moves.

```{r annual-panel}
nppes_state <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = base::c("1", "1", "1", "1", "2", "2", "2"),
  year = base::c(2020:2023, 2020:2022),
  state = base::c("CO", "CO", "CO", "CO", "NM", "NM", "TX")
)
pecos_state <- tibble::tibble(
  npi = nppes_state$npi, year = nppes_state$year,
  state = base::c("NM", "NM", "CO", "CO", "NM", "TX", "TX")
)
panels <- base::list(nppes = nppes_state, pecos = pecos_state)
universe <- dplyr::distinct(
  dplyr::bind_rows(nppes_state, pecos_state), npi, year
)
coverage <- mysteryroster::attribute_coverage(
  panels, attribute = "state", universe = universe
)
coverage$by_year
churn <- mysteryroster::attribute_churn_rate(
  pecos_state, attribute = "state"
)
churn$overall
mysteryroster::format_ranking_prose(
  group = coverage$overall$source, value = coverage$overall$pct,
  n = coverage$overall$n_total, value_label = "coverage", suffix = "%"
)$sentence
```

The lead-lag duration starts with physicians whose two sources disagree in a
specified base year. The catch-up curve instead follows the first appearances
of physician-value pairs over the whole panel. Its pooled reference starts
when any source first reports a value. A source still under observation can
contribute a censored event when it has yet to show that value. Use an external
reference with `reference = "exclude_self"` when self-confirmation would answer
the wrong study question, and declare shared lineage where applicable.

```{r timing}
duration <- mysteryroster::attribute_lead_lag_duration(
  nppes_state, pecos_state, attribute = "state",
  base_year = base::min(universe$year),
  source_a_label = "NPPES", source_b_label = "PECOS"
)
base::print(duration)
duration$b_adopts[base::c("median", "p25", "p75", "mean", "sd")]

catch_up <- mysteryroster::attribute_catch_up_curve(
  panels, attribute = "state", reference = "pooled"
)
base::print(catch_up)
catch_up$median_horizon
mysteryroster::attribute_catch_up_curve_prose(
  catch_up, display_label = base::c(nppes = "NPPES", pecos = "PECOS")
)$sentence
```

The two print calls exercise the new methods for
`mysteryroster_lead_lag_duration` and `mysteryroster_catch_up_curve`.
A missing catch-up median means the curve did not reach the 50% threshold
within the observed horizon. Timing patterns can help prioritize records
for verification.

## Report proportions and consensus predictions

Use the proportion helper for an ordinary two-sample comparison when the
groups are independent. The example below uses two separate synthetic
samples. For the same physicians measured twice, use a paired analysis.
For survey samples, use the design-based workflow above.

```{r proportions}
comparison <- mysteryroster::format_proportion_comparison_prose(
  n_a = 45, n_total_a = 100, n_b = 63, n_total_b = 100,
  label_a = "sample A", label_b = "sample B", unit_label = "records",
  condition_label = "had a populated practice ZIP"
)
comparison$combined_text
```

The truth-fusion prose helper summarizes a consensus fit, including
abstention. Treat its predictions as candidates for follow-up. Independent
verification can establish whether the predicted values are correct.

```{r consensus}
fusion_claims <- tibble::tibble(
  entity_id = base::c("1", "1", "2", "2"), attribute = "state",
  source_id = base::c("nppes", "pecos", "nppes", "pecos"),
  claimed_value = base::c("CO", "CO", "NY", "NJ"), reference_year = 2024L
)
consensus <- mysteryroster::attribute_truth_fusion(
  fusion_claims, method = "majority"
)
mysteryroster::attribute_truth_fusion_prose(
  consensus, result_label = "the synthetic practice-state fit"
)$combined_text
```
